key_insight: Equivariant graph neural networks capture 3D geometry more effectively than rotation-invariant models, improving optical spectra prediction for materials screening.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more accurate pre-screening of optoelectronic materials such as solar-cell candidates using predicted optical response instead of costly calculations.
method: Adapted GotenNet to predict optical spectra from crystal structures using equivariant message passing.
Evaluated the model on multiple datasets, including a new 10,533-structure RPA spectra collection.
Compared against current state-of-the-art surrogate models focused on scalar or lower-fidelity representations.
evidence_signal: The model outperformed prior methods, with the largest gains in the 0–8 eV range and for static real permittivity, both important for thin-film optics.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of available training spectra, so transfer to materials outside the training distribution may still be limited.
paper_title: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Improve Optical Spectra Prediction for Materials Screening
